summary: Whistler/Green Lake Water Aerodrome (YWS) is a scenic seaplane base situated on the turquoise waters of Green Lake, just minutes from Whistler Village in British Columbia. It provides a dramatic arrival route into one of North America's most celebrated mountain resort destinations, with float-equipped aircraft touching down on a glacier-fed lake framed by the Coast Mountains. The aerodrome is popular with tourists, ski packages, and visitors seeking a quick aerial link from Vancouver and other coastal hubs.
faqs:
Q: What kind of aircraft use Whistler/Green Lake Water Aerodrome?
A: Only float-equipped (seaplane) aircraft operate here, typically single and twin-engine otters and similar bush planes running scheduled and charter services.

Q: How close is the aerodrome to Whistler Village?
A: The dock is roughly 2-3 km north of Whistler Village, and most operators provide complimentary ground shuttle transfers to local hotels.

Q: Can passengers check luggage and skis?
A: Yes; operators accept checked baggage including ski and snowboard equipment, though weight and size allowances are more restrictive than on commercial airliners.

Q: Is the aerodrome open year-round?
A: Service generally runs year-round, though winter ice conditions can occasionally affect schedules and aircraft may use skis instead of floats during freeze-up.
transport_tips: Most seaplane operators include a complimentary shuttle or courtesy van to Whistler Village lodgings; confirm pickup details when booking. The dock lies along the Sea-to-Sky Highway corridor, so rental car returns and taxi services in Whistler are convenient for onward road travel. Allow at least 30 minutes for the floatplane boarding and luggage process, which is faster than a scheduled airline but still requires early arrival.
local_tip: Request a left-side window seat when booking your Vancouver-to-Whistler flight — that side lines up with the descent over Green Lake and offers the best views of the surrounding Coast Mountains and the village below.
